detail.longDescription: I have a code where some part depends on a global constant defined on top of the code (like which algorithm to use for doing my stuff). In the core of the function, if have a if statement in which some variables are defined, then later I do the same if statement to monitor values, as in this example MAGIC = True def func(): if MAGIC: a_magic = "magic" else: a_not_magic = "not magic" ... # some other stuff is done if MAGIC: print(a_magic) # "a_magic" is possibly unbound else: print(a_not_magic) # "a_not_magic" is possibly unbound Pylance in VS Code catches two errors reportPossiblyUnboundVariable , but when I execute the code, there is no issue as in all cases the variables are defined in the first if statement. (In my specific case, the second if lays inside a for loop, but I simplified for the MWE, the error is the same.) It's similar to Python/Pylance throws unexpected error "conn" is possibly unbound? , instead in my case, the variable needed in the second if will always be defined
